comments.body:
## RCA — confirmed root cause (Phase 1)

**Mechanism (proven, `dynamic`).** Every pass-health site in the live-DC tier asserts only
`"Traceback" not in cp.stderr`. `subprocess.CompletedProcess.returncode` is never read. A child
killed by a signal is terminated by the kernel *before* it can write anything, so its stderr is
the empty string; `"Traceback" not in ""` is `True` and the assertion **passes**. The pass-health
oracle therefore reports a reaped/OOM-killed reconciler pass as a healthy pass — a **fail-OPEN**
on the epic-exit evidence path.

**Discriminating experiment (runtime, 4/4 deterministic).** `.scratch/proof_failopen.py` runs a
child that `os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGKILL)`s itself, then applies the assertion **verbatim as
written at `test_dc_mutations.py:412`**:

    returncode = -9  (SIGKILL)
    stderr     = ''
    VERDICT: stderr-only assertion PASSED on a SIGKILLed child  -> FAIL OPEN

4 runs, 4 identical results. This rules out the alternative "the child still writes a partial
traceback on a signal" — it writes nothing. No Jira was contacted; the proof needs only a
subprocess.

**Intended-behavior citation (`defect_legitimacy: defect`).** The tier's own contract already
says a pass-health assertion must consult the exit status, and it predates the defective sites:

* `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py:194-203` — docstring *"Assert the run
  surfaced no traceback **and exited cleanly**"*, then `assert cp.returncode in (0, 75)`
  alongside the traceback check. Written 2026-07-30 (`6dff37c7b3`, ticket `b4e3`).
* `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_support.py:658-662` — for exactly these `run_reconcile`
  `bootstrap-strict` mutation passes: *"the pass exited N, not 0 — a failed pass's alert store
  proves nothing … only that the pass itself did not complete."* So `returncode == 0` is the
  live-proven ok-code for this pass shape.
* Closed bug `f0fb-de7a-b315-4508` fixed the same construct class in `tests/e2e`.

**Environment finding.** No live Jira DC harness on this host: `JIRA_DC_BASE_URL` defaults to
`http://localhost:2990/jira` and `curl` returns `000` (connection refused); no Jira container in
`docker ps`. `live_jira_ready()` is therefore `False` and the whole external tier self-skips.
The fail-open was proven **without** any Jira contact, and the regression test is being placed in
the unit tier so it runs in CI — a test needing live DC credentials could never gate this.

**Blast radius / scope.** The construct is NOT confined to `test_dc_mutations.py`. Repo-wide sweep
finds it across the tier: `test_dc_mutations.py` (34 sites), `test_dc_rich_text_live.py` (4),
`test_store_copy_isolation.py` (2), `_dc_fixtures.py` (1), `_dc_support.py` (1, already paired
with a returncode check). All are in scope for this fix.

## Defect origin — `caused_by`

**Origin ticket: `5200-e04e-246e-4aae`.** Class: **omission at authoring time** (`plan_defect`),
not a regression — the lines were wrong the moment they were written.

Blame on the exact implicated lines (`git blame -w -C -M`):

* `test_store_copy_isolation.py:205` → `258a463c42` *"5200: thin slice over a real scrubbed store
  copy"* (2026-08-01 02:57) — the first appearance of the half-pattern.
* `_dc_fixtures.py:333`, `test_store_copy_isolation.py:256` → `eebe86487d` (2026-08-01 08:33).
* `test_dc_mutations.py:412` and the rest → `331cfb7e88` *"5200: prove the DC mutation table
  live"* (2026-08-01 14:49), which copied the construct forward (`-C` attributes line 623 back to
  `eebe86487d`).

All three carry `rebar-ticket: 5200-e04e-246e-4aae`.

**Date test applied — and it is what makes this attribution defensible.** The implicated lines
date 2026-08-01. The *correct* form of the assertion — traceback **and** returncode — already
existed in a sibling file in the same directory since 2026-07-30 (`6dff37c7b3`, ticket `b4e3`).
So the behaviour did not become wrong through a later change: `5200` reproduced only half of an
already-established in-tier pattern. A reviewer of `5200` could plausibly have caught it, which is
the sanity check the attribution has to pass. `b4e3` is explicitly **not** the culprit — it wrote
the construct correctly and is cited above as the intended-behavior authority.

**Divergence from what blame auto-derivation would have produced.** A whole-file blame majority
over `test_dc_mutations.py` would also land on `5200`, so the culprit agrees; but the *reasoning*
differs and matters for the sweep: the earliest instance is in `test_store_copy_isolation.py`, not
in the file this bug names, and `331cfb7e88` is a carrier that copied the construct rather than
its origin. Attribution is to `5200` as the ticket whose scope of work introduced the half-pattern
across the tier.

comments.body:
## Debug report — RESOLVED (Gerrit 1989)

**Problem.** Live-DC pass-health assertions fail OPEN: a signal-killed reconciler child is
recorded as a healthy pass.

**Proven root cause.** 42 sites across the tier asserted only `"Traceback" not in cp.stderr` and
never read `cp.returncode`. A child killed by a signal is torn down by the kernel before it can
write, so its stderr is `""`, `"Traceback" not in ""` is `True`, and the assertion passes.

**Proof.** A real child that `os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGKILL)`s itself, with the assertion applied
verbatim as written at `test_dc_mutations.py:412`: `returncode=-9`, `stderr=''`, assertion
**passes** — 4/4 deterministic. This rules out the rival "a killed child still writes a partial
traceback". No Jira contact was required.

**Live DC credentials on this host: NO.** `JIRA_DC_BASE_URL` defaults to
`http://localhost:2990/jira`; `curl` returns `000` and no Jira container is running, so
`live_jira_ready()` is `False` and the tier self-skips. **Nothing was sent to any Jira instance,
read or write.** The fail-open needed only a subprocess to prove, which is also why the
regression test could be placed where CI can run it.

**Defect origin.** `caused_by` → `5200-e04e-246e-4aae`, recorded. Class: **omission at authoring
time** (`plan_defect`), not a regression. Blame on the implicated lines (`-w -C -M`) gives
`258a463c42` / `eebe86487d` / `331cfb7e88`, all carrying `rebar-ticket: 5200-e04e-246e-4aae`. The
**date test** is what makes it defensible: those lines date 2026-08-01, while the *correct* form
(traceback **and** returncode) already existed in a sibling file in the same directory from
2026-07-30 (`6dff37c7b3`, ticket `b4e3`). So nothing later broke this — `5200` reproduced only
half of an established in-tier pattern, and a reviewer of `5200` could plausibly have caught it.
`b4e3` is explicitly NOT the culprit; it is the intended-behavior authority.

**Test.** `tests/unit/test_live_dc_pass_health.py` — 6 cases. Confirmed legitimately RED first
(`DID NOT RAISE AssertionError` on 4 of 6, the right error for the right reason), then held out
of the fix subagent's working tree entirely, then GREEN 6/6 against a fix authored without
sight of it. **Mutation check:** deleting the returncode branch — the exact confirmed root cause
— returned precisely the original 4 REDs; restoring it returned GREEN. It is in the **unit**
tier deliberately: a test in the live-DC tier self-skips without a harness, which would be the
same fail-open one layer up.

**Fix.** New `tests/_child_diag.py::assert_child_ran_clean(proc, *, what, ok_codes=(0,))`. It
asserts the returncode **first** (the hole being closed; a killed child has no stderr to quote),
then the traceback. The bad-exit branch reuses `child_failure_detail` so a killed child is named
by signal — matching what bug `f0fb-de7a-b315-4508` built for `tests/e2e`, so both tiers now fail
identically. `ok_codes` defaults to `(0,)`, matching the live-proven `_dc_support.py:658`
precedent for these `bootstrap-strict` passes, and widens explicitly where a site means it (the
reconciler's legacy RESCHEDULE → exit 75).

**Scope & safety.** Test-code only; `src/` untouched. Caller-dependency sweep: the only callers
are the assertions themselves and the change is strictly stricter, so no caller depends on the
old behaviour. Restoration, not creation — it restores the contract `b4e3` set. No new
dependency (`_child_diag` is an existing in-repo helper; imports are stdlib). No test-weakening:
42 assertions removed, 45 added, no `skip`/`xfail`, and `_child_diag.py`'s diff is purely
additive so f0fb's pinned tests are untouched.

**Sweep (Step 7).** All 45 repo-wide `assert "Traceback" not in …` sites classified.
- **Fixed in scope (42):** `test_dc_mutations.py` 35, `test_dc_rich_text_live.py` 4,
  `test_store_copy_isolation.py` 2, `_dc_fixtures.py` 1 — i.e. the *whole tier*, not just the
  file this bug names.
- **Correctly left (2):** `_dc_support.py:663` and `test_reconcile_pass.py:197` already pair the
  scan with a returncode assert. They were never the bug and were not made more permissive.
- **Not siblings:** the 12 sites outside the tier are either in-process (a `CliRunner`/captured
  -stdio result cannot be signal-killed) or message-quality oracles on deliberately-failing runs
  that already pin an exit code.
- **Filed, not fixed:** `1241-b83c-f8c7-40bf` (`sound-bumpkinly-thrush`), linked
  `discovered_from` — two genuine siblings under a *different* phrasing (an absent-string oracle
  over `stdout + stderr` with no returncode check) at
  `tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py:127` and
  `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py:151`, plus a borderline `returncode != 0` at
  `tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:243` that a `-9` also satisfies. Filed
  rather than folded in: both sit outside this ticket's file lane and were held by other
  sessions.

**Replication.** The original report no longer reproduces. Driving a real SIGKILLed child through
the code now standing at `test_dc_mutations.py:412`, imported the way that module imports it:

    inbound pass did not complete: child was killed by SIGKILL (returncode -9) — some external
    process killed it rather than it failing on its own; a detached run sharing this checkout may
    have been reaped; stderr was empty

**Gates.** `make lint` (incl. complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`, config gates,
zizmor, actionlint) OK; `make typecheck` 615 files OK; all five repo-wide CI oracles
(`check_comment_hygiene`, `check_raw_git_writes`, `check_wall_clock_asserts`, `check_docs_index`,
`check_config_reads`) OK; live-DC tier still collects (74 tests); targeted guard sweep 71 passed
(`test_external_mutation_diagnostics`, `test_external_isolation`, `test_comment_hygiene_guard`,
`test_ci_workflow_parity`, `test_repo_isolation_guard`, and the new tests).

**Residual risk.** The full-tree `pytest tests` run could not be completed locally — the host was
saturated by six concurrent suites from other agents' worktrees (load average >10) and my run was
CPU-starved. **Accepted:** the change is additive to a test helper plus mechanical call-site swaps
in a self-skipping tier, the tree-scanning meta-tests that could notice it were run individually
and pass, and CI's `Verified` gate runs the exhaustive suite as the authoritative check. This is
an environment observation, not evidence about the change.

comments.body:
## Addendum — the full unit sweep did complete, and it is clean

The earlier report recorded the full-tree run as an accepted residual risk because the host was
saturated. It has since finished:

    11992 passed, 44 skipped, 1 warning, 2 errors in 2177.17s

Both `errors` are **self-inflicted concurrency artifacts, not defects** — I committed while that
suite was still running in the background:

* `test_compact_all_selection.py` — *New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT during this test:
  ['COMMITMSG.tmp']* — my temporary commit-message file, created and deleted mid-run.
* `test_compact_crash_atomicity.py` — *Test moved the repo HEAD (fe9401b1d7 -> cfbdbd3138)* — my
  own commit landing mid-run.

Both were **re-run on a quiet tree and pass: 33 passed**. So the sweep is 11992 passed with zero
real failures, and the residual risk recorded earlier is discharged.

Worth noting what those two messages demonstrate: the guards named an **external** cause instead
of blaming the straddling test. That is bug `f0fb-de7a-b315-4508`'s diagnostic fix working — the
same fix whose Step-7 sweep produced this ticket. A pleasing confirmation that the class of work
pays off in exactly the way it was argued it would.

Gerrit **1989**: `LLM-Review +1` (PASS). `Verified` still running.

compiled_state.description:
## The defect

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py` asserts reconciler-pass health with, at
17+ sites (lines 412, 467, 477, 623, 671, 728, 737, 785, 805, 892, 980, 1001, 1052, 1108,
1122, and others):

    assert "Traceback" not in cp.stderr, f"inbound pass raised:\n{cp.stderr[-2000:]}"

`cp.returncode` is never consulted. When the child is **killed by a signal** its stderr is
EMPTY, so `"Traceback" not in ""` is `True` and the assertion **passes**. A reaped or OOM-killed
reconciler pass reads as a healthy pass.

This is a **fail-OPEN** — the opposite direction from bug `f0fb-de7a-b315-4508`, where the same
missing-returncode construct produced a false *blame*. Here it produces false *green*, which is
worse: the live DC harness is the epic-exit evidence for reconciler correctness, so a silently
killed pass would be recorded as proof the pass succeeded.

## How it was found

The Step-7 construct sweep of bug `f0fb`. That bug proved (4/4 deterministic) that a
`kill -9` child yields returncode `-9` with empty stderr, and fixed the two `tests/e2e`
harness sites by routing them through a new shared helper,
`tests/_child_diag.py::child_failure_detail`, which reports the returncode and signal name.
These sites are the same construct in a tier `f0fb` did not touch.

## Why it was not fixed in scope

The `external` tier is excluded from the default run and needs live Jira DC credentials plus
`acli`, so a fix cannot be validated by the same RED->GREEN path `f0fb` used. It is also 17+
sites with a different assertion shape, and the correct remedy is a design question: assert
`cp.returncode == 0` alongside the traceback check, or route these through a shared helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A signal-killed reconciler child can no longer satisfy any pass-health assertion in
      `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py` — the returncode is checked, not only
      the stderr text.
- [x] A RED test proves it: with the child forced to die on a signal (empty stderr), the
      assertion fails before the fix and after it names the signal.
- [x] The whole file is swept — every `assert "Traceback" not in ...` site, not just the ones
      enumerated above.
- [x] Reuse `tests/_child_diag.py::child_failure_detail` rather than re-deriving the message,
      so the two tiers stay consistent.

route every stderr-only pass-health assert through the helper (the sites this bug names)
same construct, same tier - swept in scope
same construct, same tier - and the earliest instance of it
same construct in the binding fixture, which every outbound cell depends on
the RED->GREEN regression test, placed in the unit tier so CI can actually run it
